title: Tanzanian Boiled Arrowroot
author: Mama Salima
desc: Nduma za Kuchemsha — arrowroot boiled until tender and served with honey, salt, or coconut cream. An ancient Tanzanian breakfast tuber — mildly flavoured, easily digestible, and deeply traditional in the northern highlands.
longDesc: Arrowroot (nduma) is one of Tanzania's oldest cultivated foods — grown on the fertile slopes of Kilimanjaro and in highland areas. Boiled until its characteristic mildly earthy, slightly floury flesh is perfectly tender, nduma is one of the most easily digestible carbohydrates available.
steps: Place in pot with cold salted water.
Bring to a boil. Cook 20—25 minutes until a fork slides in easily.
Drain. Peel (skins peel easily after cooking).
chefTips: Cook with skin on — peels easily after.
A pinch of salt on the served arrowroot sharpens its mild flavour.
cookingScience: Arrowroot starch gelatinises at a lower temperature than potato starch, making it very easily digestible. This is why arrowroot has traditionally been used as food for the sick and the very young.
sustainabilityTips: Arrowroot is a perennial crop that regrows from rhizomes — sustainable cultivation.
healthBenefits: One of the most easily digestible starches.
culturalNote: Nduma represent Tanzania's ancient agricultural heritage — one of the oldest cultivated tubers in the East African highlands, still eaten daily in the communities that have grown them for centuries.
